Let the left and right parts of the tree be \(X=[n]\) and \(Y=[n]\). Since \(L\) preserves unions,

\[
L(S)=\bigcup_{i\in S}L(\{i\})=N(S),
\]

where \(N(S)\subseteq Y\) is the right-neighborhood of \(S\) in the bipartite tree \(G_L\). The right adjoint is therefore

\[
R(T)=\{i\in X:N(i)\subseteq T\}.
\]

Hence

\[
C(S)=RL(S)=\{i\in X:N(i)\subseteq N(S)\}.
\]

So \(S\subseteq X\) is closed iff every \(i\notin S\) has at least one neighbor outside \(N(S)\).

A useful reformulation: proper closed sets are exactly those \(S\neq X\) for which \(N(S)\neq Y\) and no outside left-vertex has all its neighbors inside \(N(S)\).

The extremal counting fact for bipartite trees with \(|X|=|Y|=n\) is:

\[
\#\{S\subsetneq X:C(S)=S\}\le 2^{n-1}.
\]

One proves this by pruning a pendant right vertex and inducting: deleting a right leaf \(y\) and its left neighbor \(x\), the remaining branches are independent once we record whether \(x\) is chosen. The closed-set condition says exactly that at least one boundary branch must remain “uncovered” unless the set is all of \(X\). This gives the recurrence

\[
g(T)\le 2^{n-2}+2^{n-2}=2^{n-1}
\]

for the number \(g(T)\) of proper closed sets. Equality occurs precisely in the rooted-star construction below. Since \(X\) itself is always closed,

\[
f(L,R)\le 2^{n-1}+1.
\]

This upper bound is sharp. Take one left vertex \(c\), connect it to every right vertex \(r_1,\dots,r_n\), and for \(i=1,\dots,n-1\), add a left leaf \(\ell_i\) adjacent only to \(r_i\). This has

\[
n+(n-1)=2n-1
\]

edges and is a tree. Every subset of \(\{\ell_1,\dots,\ell_{n-1}\}\) is closed, since \(r_n\) is not in its neighborhood, so \(c\) is not forced. Any closed set containing \(c\) has neighborhood all of \(Y\), so it closes to all of \(X\). Thus

\[
M_n=2^{n-1}+1.
\]

For the minimum, \(\varnothing\) and \(X\) are always closed. Also, because the tree has a left leaf \(\ell\), the closure of \(\{\ell\}\) is a nonempty proper closed set: it cannot be all of \(X\), since otherwise all left vertices would only see the single neighbor of \(\ell\), contradicting connectedness with \(n\ge2\). Hence always

\[
f(L,R)\ge 3.
\]

This is sharp. Let one right vertex \(r\) be adjacent to \(n-1\) left leaves \(\ell_1,\dots,\ell_{n-1}\), and let the remaining left vertex \(c\) be adjacent to every right vertex. Then the only closed sets are

\[
\varnothing,\qquad \{\ell_1,\dots,\ell_{n-1}\},\qquad X.
\]

So \(m_n=3\).

Therefore, for every \(n\ge2\),

\[
\boxed{(M_n,m_n)=\left(2^{\,n-1}+1,\ 3\right)}.
\]
